observed_reality: Current PR557 connection guard binds the main database object point-in-time and the connection-specific open WAL object to the canonical -wal path under an exact SQLite 3.53.4/Linux/x64/private-Unix-VFS probe.
The same candidate explicitly leaves productive persistence and restart/recovery unproven.
SQLite upstream documents the -shm wal-index as mmap-backed shared memory used by database clients for coordination and WAL frame lookup; it is transient and rebuildable from the WAL after crash.
No open product PR matching the searched terms 'shm wal-index' was found during this cycle.

macrocycle_unusual_experiment.name: WAL_SIDECAR_PATH_REBIND_VS_MAIN_HAS_MOVED
macrocycle_unusual_experiment.result: main SQLITE_FCNTL_HAS_MOVED remained 0 after only the live WAL pathname was rebound while existing connections retained the renamed original WAL inode; main-DB rebind sensitivity control produced HAS_MOVED=1
macrocycle_unusual_experiment.duplicate_handling: No duplicate product patch or duplicate durable WAL repair receipt was created because concurrent PR557 work already contains the WAL fd-identity repair and ordinary WAL-rebind regression.

generated_reality.hypothesis: For productive multi-connection WAL acceptance, binding the main database object and active WAL object may still be insufficient if live clients can coordinate through a different -shm/wal-index object than a newly opened client.
generated_reality.strongest_counterhypothesis: Because the wal-index is transient and controlled by SQLite's VFS/shared-memory locking semantics, an SHM pathname substitution may be unreachable, automatically rejected, or safely reconstructed without any split-coordination state; explicit SHM object pinning may therefore add complexity without safety value.
